findings.reason: The protected source is a clean disjoint-set solution with iterative path halving, union by size, and an explicit component count. Its helpers and state names are conventional, every cycle edge has a visible early exit, and no candidate is justified.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode problem 323 and its Python countComponents surface. The Reference preserves the undirected labeled-vertex model, endpoint-pair input, maximal path-connected group result, both source examples and diagrams, and all five constraints.

The immutable native source remains tied to verified submission 2064383467. Its DSU helper and Solution.countComponents adapter structurally align with the protected app-local helper and solve adapter; only the required class wrapper and legacy List annotations differ.

The legal 32, 128, and 512-vertex chain tiers span 16x and force every edge to merge a new singleton. The current source passes all nine executions at +0.01 relative growth and 1.00x; an O(n^2) whole-array relabel implementation passes all three benchmark outputs but fails only scaling at +0.99 and 46.38x.

The Approach exactly describes the initialized singleton count, root test, union-by-size update, path compression, cycle behavior, component invariant, and O(n + e alpha(n)) amortized time with O(n) space.

The hash-bound authenticated Premium Reference remains source-fidelity verified, including both source examples in order, all five constraints, and independently rendered diagrams corresponding to both source visuals.

coverage: Both authenticated source examples appear first, in source order, with their exact vertex counts, edges, and component counts.

Two illegal empty-edge cases were replaced because the source requires at least one edge and forbids self-loops; under those combined rules the smallest legal graph has two vertices joined by one edge.
Every formerly hidden graph is now a visible trial, including disjoint pairs, a spanning star, and cyclic regions joined by a bridge.
Authored trials exercise n = 2 and n = 2,000, one and 5,000 edges, endpoint labels 0 and n - 1, isolated vertices, and the maximum unique-edge count.
Cycles, dense redundant edges, bridges, stars, reversed endpoint order, and multiple disconnected components verify undirected semantics and one decrement only for distinct-root unions.

A DFS component oracle verified all 11 authored results and all three benchmark results; the protected source also matched it on all 33,861 nonempty simple undirected graphs with two through six vertices.
All 11 correctness cases are visible samples or trials; the unchanged 32-, 128-, and 512-vertex chain workloads remain hidden and performance-only in benchmark.json.
